$comment: Machine-readable enforcement policy — Agent OS v1, 2026-08-04.
Matching layer rebuilt 2026-08-04 after an adversarial review proved 22 end-to-end bypasses
and 7 false positives in the first draft. Every verified bypass string below is now a
denyExample and every verified false positive an allowExample — the canary locks both.
Macros:     __GIT__<verb> expands (in policy.mjs) to a git stem that tolerates global options
(git -C <path> push, git -c k=v push, --git-dir=…), which otherwise defeat every rule.
Preprocess: quoted -m/--message/--title/--body arguments are replaced with <ARG> before matching
(mention ≠ execution), and a single unchained read-only command (rg/grep/git log…)
Every rule MUST carry >=1 denyExamples and >=1 allowExamples; policy.test.mjs fails otherwise,
so a rule cannot ship untested and cannot be silently loosened without a red.
There is deliberately NO environment-variable bypass. If a rule must be broken, edit this file
in a PR where the diff is visible, or run the command outside the agent.

rules.why: AGENTS.md > Branching: NEVER push or commit directly to main. Named branch + PR, always.
rules.fix: git push -u origin <type>/<task>, then: gh pr create --head <branch> ; gh pr merge <n> --squash --delete-branch
denyExamples: git fetch origin ; git push origin main
allowExamples: git commit -m "docs: forbid git push origin main"

git push origin chore/x 2>&1 | tail -3
gh pr create --head chore/x --base main
git push -u origin chore/x && gh pr create --head chore/x --base main
git push origin docs/y ; gh pr merge 42 --squash --delete-branch

rules.why: AGENTS.md > Branching: never force-push shared history (any form: --force, --force-with-lease, bundled -uf, or a +refspec). Sibling sessions push to these branches. The scan stops at ;/|/& (same technique as push-to-main) so the bundled-short-flag and +refspec arms cannot reach into an unrelated chained command — witnessed 2026-09-01: `git push origin <branch> && gh api ... -f body="..."` was denied because `gh api`'s -f (field) flag matched the bundled-flag arm across the chain boundary.
rules.fix: Rebase and push normally. If a rider commit is in the way, disclose it in the PR body — never rewrite it away.
allowExamples: git push origin statenour/fix-thing && gh api graphql -f query='mutation' -f body="path matches [^/]+\.(ts|tsx)$"

rules.why: Red-team 2026-08-04: `git push`, `git push origin`, and `git push origin HEAD` resolve the destination from the CURRENT branch — which may be main. The push-to-main rule blocks a spelling; this rule blocks the destination being left implicit at all.
rules.fix: Name the full destination explicitly: git push -u origin <branch>  (or  git push origin HEAD:<branch>).

rules.why: AGENTS.md > Branching: stage only your files by explicit path. Concurrent sessions share this tree; -A/--all/. cross-contaminates apps and sweeps in sibling-session files.
denyExamples: pnpm test && git add -A && git commit -m x

rules.why: AGENTS.md > Branching: never --no-verify. The lefthook pre-commit/pre-push gate is the last check before shared history.
rules.fix: Fix what the hook is complaining about. If the check itself is wrong, change the check in a PR.

rules.why: Memory git-sync-never-reset-hard: a sibling session's uncommitted work can be sitting in this tree, and none of these leave a reflog entry for unstaged changes. Covers reset --hard, checkout -- <path>, git clean -d/-f/-x, and worktree-writing git restore.
rules.fix: Sync with: git fetch origin main ; git merge --ff-only origin/main. To discard YOUR OWN edit, copy the file aside first (cp file file.bak). git restore --staged <file> (unstage only) stays allowed.
allowExamples: git commit -m "chore: use merge --ff-only, not git reset --hard"

rules.why: Memory git-stash-pop-steals-sibling-stash: the stash is shared across worktrees. A no-op 'stash push' still exits 0, so pop/apply/branch can restore ANOTHER session's stash into your tree.
rules.fix: Copy the file aside instead (cp file file.bak), or address the stash by explicit ref after confirming it is yours (git stash list).

rules.why: AGENTS.md > Branching: node_modules in a worktree are NTFS junctions pointing OUT at the primary checkout. A recursive delete walks the links and can strip the shared node_modules every session depends on.
rules.fix: powershell scripts/worktree-teardown.ps1 -targetDir .worktrees/<name>   (unlinks junctions first, verifies targets, then removes)

rules.why: Same junction landmine as worktree-remove, reached through the shell instead of git: rm -r / Remove-Item -Recurse on a worktree directory walks the node_modules junctions into the primary checkout.
rules.fix: powershell scripts/worktree-teardown.ps1 -targetDir <worktree>   — it unlinks the junctions first.
allowExamples: Remove-Item Env:\GITHUB_TOKEN -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; gh pr list --state open
git commit -m "docs: note Remove-Item Env:\GITHUB_TOKEN false-positived in the harness sandbox"

rules.why: AGENTS.md > Protected operations: statenour migrations are hand-applied; pgvector/tsvector columns are Unsupported(...) to Prisma. --accept-data-loss silently drops them, and prisma migrate reset / db push --force-reset destroy strictly more (red-team 2026-08-04).
rules.fix: Hand-apply the migration and verify with prisma migrate status. Skill: statenour-migration.

rules.why: AGENTS.md > Protected operations: destructive schema commands need an explicit operator instruction. Memory agent-destructive-script-incident: a 'verification' run deleted 870 rows. The rule requires a DB client on the same command so that grepping/auditing SQL text stays legal — mention is not execution.
rules.fix: Ask the operator. If this is migration SQL, write it to a migration file (Write is not blocked) rather than executing it from a shell.

rules.why: Memory never-pnpm-install-in-a-junctioned-worktree: node_modules here are junctions to the PRIMARY checkout. pnpm offers to WIPE them (prompt defaults to yes), breaking every concurrent session at once.
rules.fix: Worktrees are pre-junctioned — no install needed. If deps genuinely changed, run it in the primary checkout with the '...' suffix: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --filter "<app>..."

rules.why: AGENTS.md > Protected operations: .env files hold live credentials. Agents must not author them; .env.example is the tracked contract.
rules.fix: Add the variable to .env.example and to the env validator, then ask the operator to set the real value.

rules.why: scripts/night-shift/README.md: Night Shift NEVER merges — a human merge is the only way anything ships. Until 2026-09-15 that was a sentence in a prompt while the unattended agent held the same gh authority as any session (main is unprotected, and the general instructions teach `gh pr merge`). The cwd is the identity: run.ps1 always works in .worktrees/night-shift-<date>. Also denies the ways around the front door (REST/GraphQL merge, auto-merge, /merges, rulesets, branch protection, secrets, workflow toggles).
rules.fix: Open the PR (gh pr create --head night-shift/<date> --base main ...) and stop. The operator merges — or doesn't.
denyExamples: gh api -X POST repos/o/r/merges -f base=main -f head=night-shift/2026-09-15
allowExamples: gh pr create --head night-shift/2026-09-15 --base main --title "never gh pr merge" --body "docs: the operator merges"

rules.why: A Night Shift run may push ONE thing: its own night-shift/<date> branch. Pushing to any other branch (a sibling's, a docs/ branch, a darwin/ branch) is a way to land a change outside the evaluator-separation check that keys on the branch prefix. Two arms: no night-shift ref named at all, OR any additional slash-shaped refspec that is not night-shift/ (a second refspec smuggled beside the legitimate one). push-to-main and push-implicit-dest still fire first for their own shapes.
rules.fix: git push -u origin night-shift/<date>  (the branch run.ps1 created for this run) — one refspec, nothing else
denyExamples: pnpm test && git push -u origin docs/notes
allowExamples:
git push origin night-shift/2026-09-15 2>&1 | tail -3
gh pr create --head night-shift/2026-09-15 --base main --title x --body y
git commit -m "docs: never git push -u origin main from night shift"

rules.why: config/agent-os/evaluator-paths.json: a candidate branch may change the PRODUCT, never the things that JUDGE it. CI (evaluator-separation.yml) catches this after the push; this rule catches it at the keyboard, and adds the two files that decide whether ANY guard runs at all (.claude/settings.json hooks, lefthook.yml). nightShiftPolicy.test.mjs asserts this pattern covers every path in evaluator-paths.json, so the two lists cannot drift apart silently.
rules.fix: If the right fix is an evaluator change, STOP and write it as a finding in the PR body (scripts/night-shift/PROMPT.md rule 1). A judge change is a normal branch, reviewed on its own.
